title: Canonical finite scalar realization presentations
statement: Let $T$ be a scheme and $A,B$ finite commutative unital rings in the scheme universe, with a unital ring map $f:A\to B$. Use the intrinsic constant-ring module sheaves and their ordinary unbounded derived categories on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-modules], scalar restriction $U_f$ [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and the intrinsic scalar extension $L_f$ [det-sp-scalar-extension-functor]. Write functor composites in application order, and write $E_R$ for the canonical fixed-module-to-intrinsic derived realization equivalence for $R=A,B$. Define $\widehat U_f$ and $\widehat L_f$ to be the exact derived restriction and its scalar left adjoint [def-sp-coefficient-scalar-representatives] evaluated at $f^{\mathrm{ulift}}:\operatorname{ULift}(A)\to\operatorname{ULift}(B)$; these are the existing fixedRestriction and fixedScalar. Define restrictionPresentation to be the derived exact-functor square $E_B U_f\simeq\widehat U_f E_A$ obtained by deriving the canonical realization/restriction square whose underlying maps are identity on every section. Define scalarPresentation to be the left-adjoint uniqueness isomorphism $E_A L_f\simeq\widehat L_f E_B$ determined by that restriction square. Precisely, conjugate the restriction square by $E_B^{-1}$ and $E_A^{-1}$ using the inverse counit at $B$ and inverse unit at $A$, obtaining $U_f E_A^{-1}\simeq E_B^{-1}\widehat U_f$; transport the right adjoint of $E_A L_f$ by this square and compare with the adjunction for $\widehat L_f E_B$. This specifies the comparison through its scalar units, rather than choosing an arbitrary isomorphism. No flatness or geometric finiteness hypothesis is imposed.

    (sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence T A).functor ⋙ scalarExtensionFunctor f T ≅
      fixedScalar f T ⋙ (sfIntrinsicDerivedEquivalence T B).functor
